title: Descents
key_idea: The descent set $D(w) \subseteq [n-1]$ and major index $\text{maj}(w) = \sum_{i\in D(w)} i$ are key statistics on $\mathfrak{S}_n$. The major index and the inversion number have the same distribution on $\mathfrak{S}_n$: $\sum q^{\text{maj}} = \sum q^{\text{inv}} = [n]!_q$. The Eulerian numbers $A(d,k)$ count permutations by descents.
summary: Stanley defines $\alpha(S)$ and $\beta(S)$ (counts of permutations with descent set $\subseteq S$ and $= S$), and proves Proposition 1.4.1 ($\alpha(S)$ is a multinomial coefficient). The Eulerian polynomial $A_d(x) = \sum A(d,k)x^k$ satisfies a GF formula (Prop 1.4.4-5). The major index $\text{maj}(w)$ is equidistributed with $\text{inv}(w)$ (Prop 1.4.6), proved via an elegant bijection $\varphi$ using cyclic shifts.

notation.description: Eulerian number: # permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_d$ with $k-1$ descents

definitions.statement:
For $w = w_1\cdots w_n \in \mathfrak{S}_n$, position $i$ is a **descent** if $w_i > w_{i+1}$, and an **ascent** if $w_i < w_{i+1}$. The **descent set** is $D(w) = \{i \in [n-1] : w_i > w_{i+1}\}$ and $\text{des}(w) = \#D(w)$.

The **major index** is $\text{maj}(w) = \sum_{i \in D(w)} i$ (originally called the 'greater index' by MacMahon).

The **Eulerian polynomial** in degree $d$ is $$A_d(x) = \sum_{w \in \mathfrak{S}_d} x^{1+\text{des}(w)} = \sum_{k=1}^d A(d,k)x^k$$ where $A(d,k)$ is the **Eulerian number** = $\#\{w \in \mathfrak{S}_d : \text{des}(w) = k-1\}$.

First few: $A_1=x$, $A_2=x+x^2$, $A_3=x+4x^2+x^3$, $A_4=x+11x^2+11x^3+x^4$.

propositions.title: Descent-constrained count
propositions.statement: For $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \cdots < s_k\} \subseteq [n-1]$, let $c_i = s_i - s_{i-1}$ (with $s_0=0, s_{k+1}=n$). Then $$\alpha(S) = \#\{w \in \mathfrak{S}_n : D(w) \subseteq S\} = \binom{n}{c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_{k+1}}$$
propositions.proof_sketch: A permutation $w$ with $D(w) \subseteq S$ must be increasing on each block $[s_i+1, s_{i+1}]$. Choosing which elements go in each block (then ordering them increasingly) gives the multinomial coefficient.

propositions.title: Exceedances and Eulerian numbers
propositions.statement: An **exceedance** of $w$ is a position $i$ with $w(i) > i$. The number of $w \in \mathfrak{S}_d$ with exactly $k$ exceedances equals $A(d, k+1)$ (the Eulerian number).
propositions.proof_sketch: There is a bijection between permutations with $k$ exceedances and permutations with $k$ descents, given by the Foata correspondence (the fundamental transformation of Stanley).

propositions.title: Eulerian polynomial and $m^d$
propositions.proof_sketch: Express $m^d = \sum_k k! S(d,k)\binom{m}{k}$ (via Stirling numbers of the 2nd kind) and use $\sum_m\binom{m}{k}x^m = x^k/(1-x)^{k+1}$. The resulting sum simplifies to $A_d(x)/(1-x)^{d+1}$.

propositions.title: EGF of Eulerian polynomials
propositions.proof_sketch: Differentiate the identity $\sum_m m^d x^m = A_d(x)/(1-x)^{d+1}$ with respect to $t$ after multiplying by $t^d/d!$, and use the EGF for the Bernoulli-like series.

propositions.title: Equidistribution of inv and maj
propositions.proof_sketch: Define $\varphi: \mathfrak{S}_n \to \mathfrak{S}_n$ using **cyclic shifts on compartments**: given $w$ with descent set $D(w) = \{d_1 < \cdots < d_k\}$, partition $w$ into blocks at descents and cyclically shift each block to turn descents into ascents while preserving $\text{maj}(w) = \text{inv}(\varphi(w))$. This bijection $\varphi$ satisfies $\text{inv}(\varphi(w)) = \text{maj}(w)$.

theorems.title: Bijection $\varphi$ preserves inverse descent set
theorems.statement: The bijection $\varphi$ of Proposition 1.4.6 satisfies $\text{ID}(\varphi(w)) = \text{ID}(w)$, where $\text{ID}(w) = D(w^{-1})$ is the **inverse descent set** (also called the reading set).

corollaries.title: Symmetric joint distributions
corollaries.statement: On $\mathfrak{S}_n$, the pairs $\text{(inv, maj)}$, $\text{(inv, imaj)}$, and $\text{(maj, imaj)}$ are all symmetrically jointly distributed, where $\text{imaj}(w) = \text{maj}(w^{-1})$.
corollaries.proof_sketch: Follows from Theorem 1.4.8 and the equidistribution $\text{maj} \sim \text{inv}$ applied to $w$ and $w^{-1}$.

examples.title: Example of the $\varphi$ bijection
examples.solution:
$D(w) = \{1,3,4,6,8\}$ (positions where $w_i > w_{i+1}$: $6>8$? no; $8>3$? yes at pos 2; let's reread: $w=6,8,3,9,4,1,7,2,5$).

$D(w) = \{2,4,5,7\}$ (positions 2,4,5,7 where there are descents). $\text{maj}(w) = 2+4+5+7 = 18$.

Applying $\varphi$ (cyclic shifts at compartment breaks): $\varphi(w) = 364891725$.

$\text{inv}(\varphi(w)) = 18 = \text{maj}(w)$. ✓

exercises.statement: Show that the number of permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_n$ with descent set $S$ equals $\beta(S)$, computed via inclusion-exclusion: $\beta(S) = \sum_{T \subseteq S}(-1)^{\#(S\setminus T)} \alpha(T)$.
hints: This is inclusion-exclusion on the constraint $D(w) = S$ from $D(w) \subseteq T$ for $T \subseteq S$.

text_passages.label: Definition — Descent set and major index
text_passages.preview: Position $i$ is a descent of $w$ if $w_i > w_{i+1}$. $D(w)$ = descent set. $\text{maj}(w) = \sum_{i\in D(w)} i$ is the major index (MacMahon's 'greater index').

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.4.1 — Descent-constrained count
text_passages.preview: $\alpha(S) = \#\{w: D(w) \subseteq S\} = \binom{n}{c_1,c_2,\ldots}$ where $c_i$ are consecutive differences of $S$. Proof: choose elements for each increasing block.

text_passages.label: Definition — Eulerian polynomial
text_passages.preview: $A_d(x) = \sum_{w\in\mathfrak{S}_d} x^{1+\text{des}(w)} = \sum_k A(d,k)x^k$. The Eulerian number $A(d,k)$ counts permutations with $k-1$ descents. First few: $A_3 = x+4x^2+x^3$.

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.4.4 — Power sum GF
text_passages.preview: $\sum_{m\geq 0} m^d x^m = A_d(x)/(1-x)^{d+1}$. Key identity linking Eulerian polynomials to power sums.

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.4.6 — Equidistribution of inv and maj
text_passages.preview: $\sum_{w\in\mathfrak{S}_n}q^{\text{maj}(w)} = [n]!_q$. The major index and inversion number are equidistributed on $\mathfrak{S}_n$, proved via the cyclic shift bijection $\varphi$.

text_passages.label: Theorem 1.4.8 — $\varphi$ preserves $\text{ID}$
text_passages.preview: The bijection $\varphi$ (cyclic shifts) satisfies $\text{ID}(\varphi(w)) = \text{ID}(w)$ where $\text{ID}(w) = D(w^{-1})$ is the inverse descent set.
